reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR03 campus in Hillsboro occupies 182,000 square feet of technical space. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this facility, so no IT load, critical load, or power density claim can be stated, and no rack or accelerator estimate can be derived. Without a power number, the campus cannot be ranked among Oregon's six facilities that have published capacity figures, and it falls outside the state's 182 MW published total.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only 6 have published a megawatt figure on their operator spec pages. POR03 is not among those six. That means the majority of Oregon's physical footprint, including this campus, is invisible to any analysis that depends on published power data. Hillsboro sits in Washington County, which hosts a dense cluster of data center construction driven by proximity to fiber corridors and historically favorable power rates, but none of that context changes what this page can confirm about POR03 specifically.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI workloads, the honest answer is that the published record does not support a judgment either way. Colocation space of 182,000 square feet is a meaningful physical footprint, but power capacity is the binding variable for GPU-dense deployments, and Stack Infrastructure has not published that number for POR03. The site's certifications, redundancy tier, and power density targets are also not published on the operator page as retrieved, so qualification for high-density AI training or inference hosting cannot be assessed from available data.
